The author PDF of 24 May 2023 was compared with v3 word by word: identical apart from the date and the arXiv stamp. Recomputed: α(210) for every N from 35 to 33729 (maximum 0.99211, at N = 35), the optimal exponents behind Table 1 and the ±1 case of Theorem 3.5 at 60 digits, and the E17 counterexample. The cited suppliers (Mignotte, Dobrowolski, Kolmogorov–Rogozin, Smati, Rosen, Koukoulopoulos's book, Bary-Soroker–Kozma, Łuczak–Pyber) were not re-read; they enter as items stated as the paper uses them.

summary: Bary-Soroker, Koukoulopoulos and Kozma prove that a random monic integer polynomial of degree n, with independent coefficients drawn from a fixed finitely supported law μ and non-zero constant term, has no divisor of positive degree ≤ θ(μ)n with probability 1 − O(n^{−c}) (Theorem 2), and is irreducible with Galois group A_n or S_n with that probability under Fourier conditions modulo four primes: for N ≥ 35 consecutive coefficients (Theorem 1(a)), laws with small ℓ²-norm (Theorem 3, Corollary 1(b)), odd powers (Theorem 4) and random sets (Theorem 5); for 2 to 34 consecutive values and arithmetic progressions it is irreducible with positive probability (Theorem 1(b), Theorem 3.5). The engine is joint equidistribution of the reductions modulo four primes in 𝔽_p[T] beyond the square-root barrier (Proposition 2.3), the anatomy of polynomials over 𝔽_p with a Brun sieve (Proposition 2.2), Konyagin's small-factor argument (Proposition 2.1) and a Łuczak–Pyber theorem for random partitions with a ramified Frobenius (Propositions 2.4 and 12.1). The atlas plans prime counting, sieves, finite-field character sums and Mahler measure, and Tau Ceti has polynomial Galois groups with Frobenius elements; none has random polynomials of growing degree. 133 items (15 library, 3 planned, 115 missing) are routed to Part IIs of ArithmeticStatistics (random polynomials) and of Tau Ceti's PolynomialGaloisGroups (ramified merging and random partitions) and to five source routes. Twenty-five mistakes are recorded. Among them are a lost negation in Theorem 7, a missing four-prime hypothesis in Theorem 8, an unproved exponent in Theorem 2 and false Hölder comparisons in Remark 2.2. The gaps in Lemmas 3.7 and 12.9 and in the height range of Theorem 4 are repaired.

items.name: Pointwise Fourier decay
items.statement: If |μhat_j(k/P)|≤β∈[0,1] for all P∤k and 1≤j<n, and every fraction G_p/H_p is reduced with T∤H_p, then for any q∈ℙ with ℓ_q=deg H_q≥1, σ_ℙ(n;G/H)≤β^floor((n−1)/ℓ_q).
proofSteps: Every block of ℓ_q consecutive residues contains a nonzero coefficient, or H_q would divide T^JG_q.
Use distinct-prime denominators to detect a nonzero combined character.
Bound one factor in each disjoint block by β.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Characteristic function factorization
items.statement: For every X∈𝔽_ℙ((1/T)), E exp(2πiψ_ℙ(AX))=exp(2πiψ_ℙ(T^nX))∏_{j<n}μhat_j(ψ_ℙ(T^jX)).
proofSteps: Expand AX coefficientwise.
Use independence of the integer coefficients before reduction.
Separate the deterministic monic coefficient.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Fourier reduction of congruence discrepancy
items.statement: For m≥0 and r=|ℙ|, Δ_ℙ(n;m)≤(floor(m)+1)^r Σ_{0≤ℓ_p≤m,max ℓ_p≥1}δ_ℙ(n;ℓ).
proofSteps: Apply quotient additive-character orthogonality.
Reduce B/D to G/H componentwise and split off monic gcd K.
Sum ||K||^(−1) over each possible degree, bounding it by floor(m)+1.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Torus character orthogonality
items.statement: For A∈𝔽_ℙ[T], ∫_{T_ℙ}exp(2πiψ_ℙ(AX))dX=1 if A=0 and 0 otherwise.
proofSteps: A nonzero coefficient of A gives a nontrivial finite-coordinate character.
Factor Haar measure into its uniform coefficients.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Haar finite-coordinate product identity
items.statement: For m≥0 and functions f_0,…,f_{m−1}:ℝ/ℤ→ℂ, ∫_{T_p}∏_{j<m}f_j(ψ_p(T^jX))dX=p^(−m)∏_{j<m}Σ_{ξ mod p}f_j(ξ/p).
proofSteps: The integrand is constant on balls fixing the first m coefficients.
Sum over p^m equally weighted coefficient choices.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Polynomial Farey large-sieve inequality
items.statement: For nonnegative f_0,…,f_{m−1} on ℝ/ℤ and integer ℓ≥m/2, Σ_{H monic,deg H=ℓ}Σ_{G mod H,(G,H)=1}∏_{j<m}f_j(ψ_p(T^jG/H))≤p^(2ℓ−m)∏_{j<m}Σ_{ξ mod p}f_j(ξ/p).
proofSteps: Use disjoint strict balls of radius p^(−2ℓ) around reduced fractions.
Integrand constant on each ball because m≤2ℓ.
Bound their union integral by the full Haar integral.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Iterated Fourier L1 estimate
items.statement: Let s≥1 integer, α≥0, γ≥1/2 and suppose Σ_{k mod Q}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s≤αQ^(1−γ) for every 1≤j<n,QR=P,Q>1,ℓ. If L=max_pℓ_p and m=floor((n−1)/s), then δ_ℙ(n;ℓ)≤P^max(0,L−γm) α^min(2L,m).
proofSteps: Remove the j=0 factor and incomplete block.
Hölder separates s blocks of length m; invertibility of T modulo H reindexes numerators.
Iterate Lemma 6.2 over primes ordered by ℓ_p and telescope (6.5).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Approximate joint equidistribution
items.statement: For r distinct primes with product P, n≥P^4, γ≥1/2, integer 1≤s≤n^(1/100), suppose Σ_{k mod Q}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s≤(1−n^(−1/10))Q^(1−γ) for 1≤j<n and all QR=P,Q>1,ℓ. Then Δ_ℙ(n;γn/s+n^0.88)=O_r(exp(−n^(1/10))).
proofSteps: Small L: pointwise exponential decay beats fraction count.
Middle L≤γfloor((n−1)/s): α^L supplies the decay.
Last range: P^(2+n^0.88) exp(−floor((n−1)/s)n^(−1/10)) is exponentially small.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Residue anticoncentration implies a Fourier gap
items.statement: Let P≥2 and η>0. If a probability μ on ℤ has mass≤1−η in every residue class modulo every prime dividing P, then |μhat(k/P)|≤1−4η/P² for P∤k.
proofSteps: Reduce k/P to m/Q.
Expand 1−|μhat|² as a double sum and use 1−cos(2πt)≥8||t||².
Residue-class collision probability is at most 1−η.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Fourier control bounds residue masses
items.statement: If p≥2 prime, s≥1 and Σ_{k mod p}|μhat(k/p)|^s≤p^(1−γ) with γ≥1/2, then every residue mass modulo p is≤p^(−γ/s)≤2^(−1/(2s))≤1−1/(4s).
proofSteps: Fourier inversion followed by Hölder bounds each residue mass.
The final elementary inequality holds for s≥1.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Small irreducible factors are rare
items.statement: For support μ_j⊂[−exp(n^(1/3)),exp(n^(1/3))], ||μ_j||∞≤1−n^(−1/10) for 1≤j<n, and μ_0 not concentrated at 0, conditional probability given a_0≠0 of an irreducible factor of degree≤n^(1/10) is O(n^(−7/20)), with absolute constant.
proofSteps: Condition only μ_0.
Cyclotomic factors use root anticoncentration and the inverse-totient count.
Noncyclotomic factors use degree-preserving prime powers and Mahler measure to force unique sparse coefficients, then union-bound exp(n^0.54) candidates against exp(−n^0.55).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Four-prime irreducibility criterion
items.statement: Let ε∈(0,1/100], θ∈(0,1/2], λ0=1/(4−4log2). Assume coefficient supports in ±exp(n^(1/3)); four distinct primes ℙ; Δ_ℙ(n;θn+n^(λ0+ε))≤n^(−30); and, for 1≤j<n, ||μ_j||∞≤1−n^(−1/10), Σ_{a≡0 mod p}μ_j(a)≤1−n^(−ε/200) for every p∈ℙ. Then P(Bad_{θn}(A) AND a_0≠0)≤C(ε)n^(−c(ε)) for some positive C,c depending only on ε.
proofSteps: Apply small-factor bound to the joint event without conditioning Δ.
On the smooth-part good event, sum the four-prime divisor bound over n^0.1≤k≤θn.
Use 4(1−log 2−ε/10)(λ0+ε)≥1+0.8ε; keep the small-factor error n^(−7/20), not the printed n^(−2/5).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Master small-factor theorem, corrected event
items.statement: Assume every support lies in ±exp(n^(1/3)), μ_0≠δ_0, P≤n^(1/4) is a product of four distinct primes, γ≥1/2 and integer 1≤s≤n^(1/20000)/4. Assume the Fourier inequality in item 24 for all 1≤j<n. Put θ=γ/s. Then P(Bad_{θn}(A)|a_0≠0)≤C_1 n^(−c) for absolute c,C_1>0. Equivalently, absence of such nonconstant divisors has probability at least 1−C_1n^(−c).
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 7 pp. 13–14, corrected E1
proofSteps: Replace μ_0 by its nonzero-conditioned law; the Fourier premise omits j=0.
Apply Proposition 2.3 and then 2.2 with θ clipped at 1/2.
γ<1 follows from μhat(0)=1; irreducibility covers the clipped case θ>1/2.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: One-prime large-Galois criterion
items.statement: For ε>0, a prime p and coefficient laws, assume Δ_p(n;n/2+n^(λ0+ε))≤n^(−10) and every μ_j,1≤j<n, has mass≤1−1/(log n)² in the zero residue class mod p. Then P(A irreducible AND G_A∉{A_n,S_n})≤C(ε)n^(−c(ε)). This is an unconditional joint probability, not P(bad Galois|irreducible).
proofSteps: For an irreducible A, use separability and a ramified Frobenius lift.
Large multiplicities have probability O(1/n).
Otherwise a bad transitive group supplies a small-merging partition excluded by Lemma 11.6.
For general ε>0, run the small-ε proof with ε′=min(ε/2,1/100); Δ is monotone in its degree cutoff.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Four-prime Galois master theorem, corrected hypothesis
items.statement: Assume supports in ±exp(n^(1/3)); P≤n^(1/4) is the product of four distinct primes; and Σ_{k mod Q}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|≤(1−n^(−1/10))Q^(1/2) for 0≤j<n and all QR=P,Q>1,ℓ. Then P(G_A∈{A_n,S_n}|a_0≠0)=1−O(n^(−c)) for an absolute c>0.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 8 p. 16, corrected E2
proofSteps: The j=0 Fourier bound gives P(a_0≠0)≥1/4, making conditioning harmless up to an absolute factor.
Apply Theorem 7 with s=1,γ=1/2 and Proposition 2.4 to any p|P.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Consecutive intervals of size at least 35
items.statement: There exist absolute c>0,n0 such that, for H≥1, an N-element interval of consecutive integers Nset⊂[−H,H], N≥35, and n≥max(n0,(log H)^3), a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) is irreducible with probability≥1−n^(−c).
proofSteps: Use the certified uniform α(210)<1 for n large enough to meet the Fourier margin and P^4 bound.
For the large-N/small-n regime use Lemma 3.1 as in the source.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Short consecutive intervals have positive irreducibility probability
items.statement: There exist absolute δ>0,n0 such that, for H≥1, a consecutive interval Nset⊂[−H,H] with 2≤N≤34 and n≥max(n0,(log H)^3), a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) is irreducible with probability≥δ.
proofSteps: For each N in 2,…,34 take s_N from Table 1 and any γ with 1/2 ≤ γ < γ(s_N) (/132; the printed γ are rounded, E20).
Combine exclusion of small factors with the positive lower bound for absence of medium factors.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: General finite laws: verified weaker quantitative parameter
items.statement: For integers H,n≥3 and iid μ supported on [−H,H] with ||μ||∞≤1−ε, 0<ε<1, there exist absolute c,C,c′>0 such that, when n≥C ε^(−20000)(log H)^(1000000), all nonconstant divisors have degree≥θn with conditional probability≥1−n^(−c), where the argument verified here supplies θ=c′ε/(log H)^9. The source's stronger exponent 5 remains an unresolved target, not an established correction.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 2 p. 3 and §3.5 p. 25; E4
proofSteps: Put x=log(2H+1). CRT plus a union bound finds four primes in (x,3x] with residue masses≤1−εlogx/(3x).
Lemma 3.6 supplies a Fourier gap at least cεlogx/x^9, since P≤(3x)^4.
Choose s=ceil(Cε^(−1)x^9) so the total Fourier s-norm is<2^(1/4), then apply Theorem 7.
The printed degree threshold with exponent 10^6 is more than sufficient; only the explicit θ exponent 5 is not justified.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.
items.sourceClaim: Printed θ=c′ε/(log H)^5; retained as a target blocked by E4, not silently replaced as an equivalent theorem.

items.name: Sparse-support l2 criterion
items.statement: For iid μ on ℤ, integers H,n≥3, supp μ⊂[−H,H] and ||μ||_2²≤min(H^(−4/5),n^(1/16)/H)/(log H)^2, there are absolute c>0,H0≥3 such that H≥H0 implies P(A irreducible|a_0≠0)≥1−n^(−c).
proofSteps: Choose x≈HlogH/N; the large-sieve average supplies four primes with α(P)≤1/2.
N≥H^(4/5)(log H)^2 makes the parameter interval nonempty and n≥(H/N)^16(log H)^32 implies P^4≤n.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Arbitrary finite sets: small-factor exclusion
items.statement: There are absolute c>0,n0≥3 and θ(H)>0 such that for integers H,n≥3, any Nset⊂[−H,H] with N≥2, and n≥max(n0,(log H)^3), a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) has every nonconstant divisor of degree≥θ(H)n with probability≥1−n^(−c).
proofSteps: Use ε=1/2 in the general finite-law theorem.
Shrink θ(H) further so θ(H)n<1 below its H-dependent large-degree threshold; the assertion there is deterministic.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Large arbitrary finite sets: irreducibility
items.statement: For absolute c>0,H0≥3, integers H,n≥3, Nset⊂[−H,H] with N≥H^(4/5)(log H)^2, H≥H0 and n≥(H/N)^16(log H)^32, a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) is irreducible with probability≥1−n^(−c).
proofSteps: Uniform-on-Nset has ||μ||_2²=1/N.
Substitute directly into Theorem 3.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Odd-power coefficient sets
items.statement: For every positive odd integer d there exist H0(d),n0(d)≥3 and an absolute c>0 such that H≥H0(d), n≥max(n0(d),(log H)^3), and uniform A∈Υ_{ {k^d:1≤k≤H} }(n) imply irreducibility probability≥1−n^(−c).
proofSteps: Choose four primes with gcd(p−1,d)=1; the power map is bijective on each residue field.
Bound incomplete residue blocks to get α(P)<1 for H sufficiently large; use H≥3P(P−1), correcting E5.
The coefficients k^d lie in [1, H^d] ⊆ [−exp(dn^(1/3)), exp(dn^(1/3))] when n ≥ (log H)^3; apply Theorem 7 with this support bound (/131), valid for n ≥ n_0(d). This repairs E18.
items.note: Positive d and integer coefficient model are explicit; negative odd exponents do not define the stated integer family.

items.name: A random coefficient set is usually good
items.statement: For H≥1 and integer 2≤N≤|[−H,H]∩ℤ|, choose Nset uniformly among N-element subsets of [−H,H]∩ℤ. There are absolute c>0,n0≥1 such that, with set-probability at least 1−O(N^(−1/2)), for every n≥max(n0,(log H)^3) the conditional uniform polynomial law on Υ_Nset(n) has irreducibility probability≥1−n^(−c).
proofSteps: Bound EΣ_{k=1}^{209}|μhat_Nset(k/210)| by O(N^(−1/2)).
Markov gives α(210)≤3/4 outside O(N^(−1/2)) bad sets.
The good-set property is fixed before n varies.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Alternating or symmetric groups with high probability
items.statement: In the coefficient regimes of items 32,35,38,39, the Galois action of A on its n roots, conditioned on a_0≠0, is A_n or S_n with probability≥1−n^(−c) for an absolute c>0. For item 39 the assertion is inside the same good-set event.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 6 first part p. 5; §3.7 p. 28
proofSteps: Each proof supplies a four-prime α(P)≤1−c0 with P≤n^(1/4).
Invoke the Galois master theorem; see E10 for the printed reciprocal exponent.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Alternating or symmetric groups for short intervals
items.statement: In the setting of item 33, the Galois action is A_n or S_n with probability≥δ−n^(−c), after decreasing the absolute δ,c if needed.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 6 second part p. 5; §3.7 p. 28
proofSteps: Choose a prime p dividing N; all unconditioned coefficients are uniform mod p, so Δ_p=0.
Apply Proposition 2.4 to the unconditional law, then divide its bad-event bound by P(a_0≠0)≥1/2.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: k-fold irreducibility
items.statement: For a separable degree-n polynomial A∈ℚ[T] and 1≤k≤n, say it is k-fold irreducible when A is irreducible and, for every 1≤j<k, deleting j distinct roots leaves a polynomial irreducible over the field generated by those roots. Multiplication by the leading-coefficient unit does not affect irreducibility.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: k-fold irreducibility and multiple transitivity

proofSteps: At each tower stage, the stabilizer of the chosen roots is the Galois group of the splitting extension over their field.
Transitivity on the remaining roots is equivalent to irreducibility of the residual polynomial.
Iterate using ordered injective root tuples.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: High-order irreducibility, corrected scope

items.name: Exact Fourier spectrum of a consecutive interval
items.statement: For μ uniform on {a,…,a+N−1}, P≥2 and 1≤k<P, |μhat(k/P)|=|sin(πNk/P)|/(N sin(πk/P)); μhat(0)=1. If N≡r mod P, the numerator depends only on r and k.
proofSteps: Sum the finite geometric progression.
Translation contributes a phase only.
Take moduli and use |1−exp(2πit)|=2|sinπt|.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Exact certificate for all N≥35
items.statement: For μ uniform on any consecutive N integers with N≥35, α(210)^2<997/1000<1. It suffices to verify the finite set N=35,…,244 because, within each residue class mod 210, every nonzero-frequency modulus in item 46 decreases with N and the zero-frequency term stays 1.
items.locator: arXiv v3, §3.1 pp. 17–18; extraction certificate C1
proofSteps: For each Q|210,Q>1 and ℓ mod (210/Q), use frequency indices kR+ℓQ mod 210.
Bound π by Machin's arctangent identity and each sine by alternating Taylor polynomials on [0,π/2].
Sum upward-rounded rational bounds and verify S²<Q·10^70 in 76860 cases.
items.note: A proved finite-reduction argument plus executed exact-rational certificate; not a Lean theorem. Complete executable certificate is embedded in the report.

items.name: Large interval, small degree
items.statement: If Nset is an interval of N consecutive integers contained in [−N^(loglog(100N)),N^(loglog(100N))], and n≤N^(1/200), then the reducible proportion of Υ_Nset(n) is O(N^(−3/10)), with absolute implied constant.
proofSteps: Bound the number of possible nonzero factor constant terms by the divisor function.
Count possible monic factor pairs modulo N by their degrees and lift the coefficient interval uniquely.
Use the maximal-order divisor bound uniformly over the support.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Medium-factor exclusion using an exactly uniform prime
items.statement: For an N-element arithmetic progression Nset of step d, N≥2, a prime p|N with p∤d, and θ∈[0,1/2], the proportion of Υ_Nset(n) with no nonconstant divisor of degree in [θn,n/2] is at least−log(1−θ)+O(1/n), with an absolute implied constant.
proofSteps: Modulo p count products D·I, where I irreducible of degree n−m>n/2 and m<θn.
Treat m=0 separately, correcting E6, and use the fixed-nonzero-constant prime-polynomial estimate for m≥1.
Distinct large irreducible factors give disjoint representations; sum the harmonic terms.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Medium-factor exclusion for any progression
items.statement: For an N-element arithmetic progression Nset⊂[−H,H] with N≥2 and θ∈[0,1/2], the proportion of Υ_Nset(n) without a divisor of degree in [θn,n/2] is at least−log(1−θ)−O(log(nH)/(sqrt(n)log N)).
proofSteps: Evaluate at the radix N, a bijection on each fixed-constant slice.
Discard the unique possible zero evaluation (E7).
A sufficiently large prime divisor of the nonzero value forces a factor of degree>(1−θ)n by Lemma 3.4.
Count such values using primes in progressions and Mertens estimates.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Evaluation bound for an irreducible integral factor
items.statement: If A∈ℤ[T] has degree n, all coefficients bounded by H≥1, and an irreducible monic factor I of degree m divides A, then for integer N≥2, |I(N)|≤N^m exp(4(1+sqrt(m))log(14sqrt(n)H)).
proofSteps: Apply the source's stronger Mignotte l2 bound to I, not just the binomial coefficient bound.
Cauchy–Schwarz bounds evaluation at N.
Enlarge constants to the displayed uniform envelope.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Positive irreducibility for arbitrary arithmetic progressions
items.statement: Let Nset⊂[−H,H] be an N-element arithmetic progression of step d≥1 with N≥2. Let P be the product of the four smallest primes not dividing d. There exist δ(P)>0,n0(P) such that n≥max(n0(P),(log H)^3) implies a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) is irreducible with probability≥δ(P). For Nset={−1,1} one can take P=1155, s=735, any γ slightly below γ(735)=0.5000197007327… (/132) and δ=0.00068053.
proofSteps: Nonconcentration modulo primes not dividing d gives a finite Fourier exponent s.
Use small-factor exclusion and medium-factor exclusion.
For Nset={−1,1} use P=1155 and s=735 with γ just below γ(735); the printed γ equals γ(735), where α=1 exactly (E20).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Random-set Fourier second moment
items.statement: For a uniform N-element subset S of {−H,…,H}, H∈ℕ,N≤2H+1, and θ=k/210 with 1≤k≤209, let δ1=N/(2H+1),δ2=N(N−1)/(2H(2H+1)). Then E|Σ_{a∈S}e(aθ)|²=δ2|Σ_{a=−H}^H e(aθ)|²+(δ1−δ2)(2H+1)=O(N). Consequently EΣ_{k=1}^{209}|μhat_S(k/210)|=O(N^(−1/2)).
proofSteps: Separate diagonal and off-diagonal pairs in the uniform subset model.
Bound the complete interval geometric sum at each of 209 fixed nonzero frequencies.
Apply Cauchy–Schwarz and divide by N.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Four-prime average from the large sieve
items.statement: For x≥2,H≥1 and μ supported on [−H,H], let N_4(x) be the products of four distinct primes in [x/2,x]. Then Σ_{P∈N_4(x)}α(P)≪(x/log x)^4·((xlogx)^2+sqrt(Hlogx/x))·||μ||_2, with an absolute constant.
proofSteps: Reduce frequency fractions k/Q and ℓ/R.
Twice use Cauchy–Schwarz and CRT to obtain reduced rational frequencies of denominator≤x^(i1+j1).
Apply the additive large sieve and maximize the finitely many exponents.

In the change of variables q=Q_1R_1 keep Q_1∈N_{i_1}(x) and R_1∈N_{j_1}(x); each q then has at most C(i_1+j_1,i_1)≤6 such factorizations. Enlarging to all Q_1≤x^(i_1), R_1≤x^(j_1) loses a factor up to 2^ω(q) (E19).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

Here ||·||_2 is the Euclidean norm of the full coefficient vector. This is the exact inequality displayed in BKK23; its hypotheses and proof in Mignotte 1988 remain a source gate.

items.name: Cauchy bounds away from zero

If |z|≤1/(H+1), the nonzero integer constant term dominates.

items.name: Bounded small-factor coefficient universe

items.name: Root anticoncentration, complex case repaired
items.statement: If ||μ_j||∞≤1−ε for 1≤j<n, n≥2 and ε>0, then for every nonzero complex z, P(A(z)=0)≪1/sqrt(εn), with an absolute constant.
proofSteps: Choose a real-linear projection L:ℂ→ℝ with L(z^j)≠0 for every 1≤j<n, avoiding finitely many bad directions.
Project A(z)=0 and set δ=(1/2)min_{1≤j<n}|L(z^j)|>0. Then Q(a_j L(z^j);δ)≤||μ_j||∞.

items.name: Few primes drop algebraic degree
items.statement: For a nonzero algebraic number α of degree m over ℚ, at most log m/log 2 primes p satisfy[ℚ(α^p):ℚ]<m. Consequently, for H=floor(exp(n^(1/3))) and m≤n^0.1, there is for n sufficiently large a prime L(m)log(2Hn)<p≤2L(m)log(2Hn) for which α^p retains degree m.

items.name: Sparse coefficient uniqueness
items.statement: Let D be a monic noncyclotomic irreducible integer polynomial with nonzero roots z_i, and let p be a prime such that the z_i^p are distinct and p>L(m)log(2Hn), with M(D)≥exp(1/L(m)). Given all a_j for 0≤j<n with p∤j, at most one monic degree-n A with |a_j|≤H and D|A has those coefficients.
proofSteps: Two choices differ by G(T^p), with nonzero integer G and coefficients≤2H.
Divide G by its nonzero integer leading coefficient to make it monic.
Distinct roots z_i^p force M(G/lc G)≥M(D)^p>2Hn, while the coefficient-sum bound is≤2Hn.

items.name: Prime-polynomial bounds
items.statement: For a prime p and integer k≥1, if π_p(k) counts monic irreducible degree-k polynomials over 𝔽_p, then (p^k−2p^(k/2))/k≤π_p(k)≤p^k/k. Hence Σ_{deg I=k}1/||I||_p≤1/k.

items.name: Squarefree Bonferroni sieve inequality
items.statement: If B is squarefree and v≥1 integer, then Σ_{G|B,ω(G)≤2v−1}(−1)^ω(G)≤1_{B=1}≤Σ_{G|B,ω(G)≤2v}(−1)^ω(G). Here divisors are monic and ω counts distinct irreducible factors.
proofSteps: Identify divisors with subsets of irreducible factors.
Apply the finite alternating binomial partial-sum identity.

items.name: Brun upper bound for general joint polynomial laws
items.statement: Let ℙ contain r primes and let ν be any law on M_ℙ(n). For monic D_p and selected irreducibles I_p of degrees≤ℓ_p with ℓ_p≥11, ν(D|A,(A/D,I)=1)≤(2^r/||D||)∏_{p,J∈I_p}(1−1/||J||)+Σ_{G|I,ω(G_p)≤6logℓ_p ∀p}|ν(DG|A)−1/||DG|| |. Every G_p in the remainder has degree≤6ℓ_p log ℓ_p.
proofSteps: Truncate inclusion-exclusion at 2v_p with v_p=ceil(3/2+2logℓ_p); all upper sums are nonnegative, permitting multiplication.
Compare the truncated main term with its Euler product.
Bound the tail by 1/(2v_p+1)! times a reciprocal-prime sum power, and use (e/4)^(4x)≤1−x for 0≤x≤1/2.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Small-prime Euler product bound
items.statement: For m≥0 integer and prime p, let I be all monic irreducibles J≠T of degree≤m. Then ∏_{J∈I}(1−1/||J||_p)≤2/(m+1).
proofSteps: Expand the inverse Euler product over smooth monic polynomials.
Keep all degrees 0,…,m, contributing m+1 after normalization, and account for the removed factor T by (1−1/p)≥1/2.

items.statement: Fix C≥1, prime p, integer n≥3, integer 4C≤m≤n and u≥2. For arbitrary independent coefficient laws, P(deg A_p^S(m)>um)≤O_C(m exp(−Cu))+Δ_p(n;um).

items.name: Generalized Łuczak–Pyber theorem

items.name: Imprimitive-group exclusion
items.statement: For n≥n_0, 0≤θ≤δ/2−ε and ρ∈E1∩…∩E5 (E5 as in /108), no g∈Merge(ρ;n^θ) lies in a transitive imprimitive subgroup of S_n.
proofSteps: Let the blocks have size s=n/r. For a cycle L_ℓ of g coming from a part ℓ of multiplicity one, let X_ℓ be the union of the r′_ℓ blocks it meets and s′_ℓ=ℓ/r′_ℓ. X_ℓ is one orbit of g on blocks, every cycle of g in X_ℓ has length divisible by r′_ℓ, and X_ℓ∖L_ℓ≠∅ iff s′_ℓ<s.
Case 2≤r≤n^(δ/2): as in the paper, via E5 and E2.

Case n^(δ/2)<r<n^(1−α): E1 and E3 give five distinct parts ℓ in [n^(1−α),n/log n]. Here r′_ℓ≥ℓ/s>n^(δ/2−α)≥n^α, so X_ℓ=X_ℓ′ would give gcd(ℓ,ℓ′)>n^α; the X_ℓ are disjoint. At most one ℓ has s′_ℓ=s (Case 2a) and g has at most three cycles longer than n/4, so some ℓ has s′_ℓ<s and only cycles of length ≤n/4 in X_ℓ∖L_ℓ. Such a cycle has length mk with m≤n^θ, k≤n/4, and r′_ℓ|mk gives gcd(k,ℓ)>n^(δ/2−α−θ)=n^α, contradicting E1.

Case n^(1−α)≤r<n: E5 (/108) gives four distinct parts ℓ in [n^(1−2α),n/log n] with s∤ℓ, hence s′_ℓ<s and r′_ℓ>n^(1−3α). The same disjointness and counting give a cycle of length mk≤n/4 in some X_ℓ∖L_ℓ with gcd(k,ℓ)≥r′_ℓ/m>n^(1−3α−θ)≥n^(κα), contradicting E1.

items.name: Small-factor exclusion for supports up to exp(Cn^(1/3))
items.statement: Fix C ≥ 1. Let μ_0,…,μ_{n−1} be probability measures on ℤ with supp(μ_j) ⊆ [−exp(Cn^(1/3)), exp(Cn^(1/3))] for all j, ‖μ_j‖_∞ ≤ 1−n^(−1/10) for 1 ≤ j < n, and supp(μ_0) ≠ {0}. Then, for n ≥ n_0(C), P_{M(n)}(A has an irreducible factor of degree ≤ n^(1/10) | a_0 ≠ 0) ≪ n^(−7/20). Consequently Theorems 7 and 8 (/29, /31) hold with condition (a) replaced by the support bound exp(Cn^(1/3)), with n_0 depending on C.
items.locator: §7, pp. 35–38 (the proof of Proposition 2.1, run with H = ⌊exp(Cn^(1/3))⌋); needed for Theorem 4, §3.3, p. 23 (E18)
proofSteps: Claim 7.1 and the height bound (7.1) hold verbatim with H = ⌊exp(Cn^(1/3))⌋; they need only n ≤ H.
The Dobrowolski prime satisfies p ≤ 2L(m)log(2Hn) ≪ Cn^(1/3)(log n)^3, so for each non-cyclotomic D, P(D|A) ≤ (1−n^(−1/10))^⌊(n−1)/p⌋ ≤ exp(−c n^(17/30)/(C (log n)^3)).

#D(n^(1/10)) ≤ 2(2(H+1)^(m_0)+1)^(m_0) ≤ exp(O(Cn^(8/15))) with m_0 = ⌊n^(1/10)⌋; since 8/15 < 17/30 the union bound is o(n^(−7/20)) once n ≥ n_0(C). The cyclotomic term (Lemma 7.3) does not involve the support.
Condition (a) of Theorems 7 and 8 enters their proofs only through Proposition 2.1 (in §10), so they extend.
items.note: Worker repair of E18 in this continuation, not a statement of the paper. With C = d it gives Theorem 4 (/38) in the printed range n ≥ max(n_0(d),(log H)^3).

items.name: Large Galois group for arithmetic-progression coefficients
items.statement: Let 𝒩 ⊂ [−H,H] be an arithmetic progression of step d with N ≥ 2 elements, and suppose some prime p divides N but not d. With P, δ = δ(P) and n_0(P) as in Theorem 3.5 (/52), for n ≥ max(n_0,(log H)^3) a uniformly random A ∈ Υ_𝒩(n) has Galois group A_n or S_n with probability ≥ δ − n^(−c), for an absolute c > 0.
proofSteps: For 1 ≤ j < n the coefficient a_j mod p is uniform, since p | N and p ∤ d.
For D coprime to T with deg D < n, the classes T,…,T^(deg D) span 𝔽_p[T]/D, so A_p mod D is uniform whatever the law of a_0: Δ_p(n; n/2+n^λ) = 0.
The zero class has mass 1/p ≤ 1/2 for j ≥ 1, so Proposition 2.4 (/30, with Lemma 11.5 in the form /101) bounds P(A irreducible, G_A ∉ {A_n, S_n}) by Cn^(−c); combine with Theorem 3.5.
items.note: The paper states this in Remark 3.3 without a separate proof and notes that it does not cover 𝒩 = {−1, 1}.

routes.title: Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions, Part II: random polynomials of growing degree
routes.reason: ST.0–5 organize height/discriminant-ordered number fields, Selmer averages and class-group laws; they do not plan growing-degree independent-coefficient polynomial laws. The new probability space and uniform n,H,μ estimates need new layers. PM supplies generic concentration; this route owns only its polynomial applications.
routes.brief: Build on Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions (ArithmeticStatistics), importing its counting/probability conventions without recasting these laws as discriminant-ordered fields. The endpoints are the exact statements in items 29–41, 44–45, 52, 123 and 133; keep all conditioning, n/H ranges and absolute versus d-dependent constants. Specifically obtain probability≥1−n^(−c) for irreducibility of uniform consecutive N-element coefficient intervals when N≥35 and n≥max(n₀,(log H)^3); for 2≤N≤34 obtain an absolute positive lower bound. Import the exact Fourier certificate 47 and the Table 1 and ±1 certificates 132 (use γ below the optimal γ(s), not the rounded printed values). For general iid laws with mass≤1−ε, the presently justified small-factor cutoff is cεn/(log H)^9 under n≥Cε^(−20000)(log H)^1000000; the paper's exponent 5 remains E4, not a proved target. The l2 criterion is ||μ||₂²≤min(H^(−4/5),n^(1/16)/H)/(log H)^2. Odd-power sets, random sets and the other endpoints must retain their item-specific hypotheses and gates. Construct monic coefficient PMFs, CRT joint reductions, σ,δ,Δ, smooth/rough parts excluding T, additive statistics and conditional-law adapters with the APIs/tests in each definition. Prove small-factor exclusion, Fourier equidistribution, four-prime summability and the partition law bounds before applications. Import Finite fields, character sums, finite rings and coding interfaces (FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums) for residue duality and prime-polynomial estimates; Sieve methods, prime gaps and prime patterns (SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns) for both large sieves and Brun; Classical arithmetic, sequences, polynomials and reciprocity (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion) for sharper Mignotte and Dobrowolski; Analytic number theory, zeta functions and prime distribution (AnalyticNumberTheory) for prime and totient estimates; Probabilistic, metric and ergodic number theory (ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory) for concentration. Import the proposed PolynomialGaloisGroupsPartIIRandomPartitions only for the deterministic/group criterion; it must not import this route's final Galois theorem in return. The imprimitive-group step (E12) and the odd-power height range (E18) are repaired here: item 117 and item 131, which extends the small-factor estimate to supports exp(Cn^(1/3)). No exponentially small reducibility error, universal S_n rather than A_n-or-S_n, or general-law irreducibility is claimed. Suggested eventual module: TauCeti/Probability/RandomPolynomial/GeneralMeasures.lean; no Lean file is delivered by this paper job.

routes.title: Galois groups of polynomials, Part II: ramified merging and random partitions
routes.reason: The upstream roadmap already owns permutation representations, block systems and good-prime Frobenius specialization. The new layer is bounded equal-part merging at ramified primes and a quantitative random-partition obstruction to proper transitive subgroups; none of the existing carriers is re-planned.
routes.brief: Extend Galois groups of polynomials (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PolynomialGaloisGroups), importing its layers 0,1,5 and 9. Reuse the pinned Polynomial.Gal action, fullCycleType, factorDegrees, arithmetic Frobenius existence at ramified primes and finite-field orbit/factor theorems. Prove item 100: for irreducible integral monic A and every prime p, some Galois element has cycle type obtained by merging equal parts of the mod-p factorization partition, with each merged block bounded by the maximum factor multiplicity. Do not replace this by an unramified-prime assertion. Then build the arbitrary partition-law criterion 103, with all three probability premises, C,t,κ,δ and ε∈(0,δ/2). Its endpoint is ν(Merge(ρ;n^θ)∩T_n≠∅)≪(log n)^2n^(−κ(δ/4−θ/2)) uniformly 0≤θ≤δ/2−ε; T_n is the union of proper transitive subgroups excluding A_n and S_n. E₁ controls only pairs of parts ≤n/4, so the imprimitive case follows item 117: the block orbits of five long parts are disjoint and at most three cycles exceed n/4, and E₅ is strengthened to four long parts not divisible by any r≥2 (item 108), with the same probability bound (item 113). Define multiset subset and equal-part merging precisely; expose all E₁–E₅ thresholds, fixed points, multiplicity and min-support conventions. Import AnalyticNumberTheory divisor/Mertens estimates and the original primitive-group minimum-degree theorem, not an unproved Jordan-theorem shortcut. ArithmeticStatisticsPartIIRandomPolynomials supplies concrete coefficient-law instances only AFTER this arbitrary-law criterion; avoid a roadmap-level circular final theorem. Also prove the distinct-root, k-fold-irreducibility versus k-transitivity adapter and its (n−2)-fold consequence for n≥3. The construction must test identity/full cycle type, repeated mod-p factors, unit polynomial and nonseparable counterexamples. Suggested eventual modules: TauCeti/GroupTheory/Perm/RandomPartitions.lean and TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/RamifiedMerging.lean; no new Lean is claimed here.

routes.reason: FF.1/4 own exact additive-character and finite harmonic-analysis interfaces. FF.3 receives prime-polynomial enumeration and its factorization-based proof, including degree 1. BKK is a consumer/source locator, not a replacement for Rosen's full proof.

Only the sharper sqrt(m)-exponent factor norm, its evaluation adapter, Dobrowolski and prime-power degree-drop input remain; no general Lehmer lower bound is asserted.

AN.2 owns prime counts and counts of fixed-size products of medium primes; AN.5 supplies inverse-totient/divisor/Mertens estimates. Already-built Dirichlet infinitude is imported, not replanned and not confused with PNT. The items state these suppliers as the paper uses them; their proofs belong to the layers' blueprints.

Add the concentration function and general real independent-sum bound there as a reusable supplier; do not invent a random-polynomial-specific Kolmogorov–Rogozin theorem. The reviewed audit says generic probability/moments are built, not that this concentration estimate is built. Other consumers include bounded-digit and additive-arithmetic laws; the polynomial root projection remains in the random-polynomial Part II.
